title.narrative: Output 3.2. Increased capacity of member States to formulate and implement policies and strategies for creating decent work in the rural economy

description.narrative: The Government of South Africa included pro-employment and climate smart principles and approaches in the national public employment programme. These involved the realignment of programme strategy towards creating more and better jobs as well as climate proofing of existing and new infrastructure as part of greening the Expanded Public Works Progamme (EPWP), The above approaches are currently being rolled out in the provinces and rural and district municipalities with particular focus on the rural areas. Government developed and adopted an infrastructure led Economic Reconstruction and Recovery Plan in June 2021, aimed at reducing the socio-economic impact of COVID- 19 pandemic incorporating ILO inputs on maximizing employment through public works in rural and peri-urban areas. During the biennium, with the support of the Government of South Africa, the ILO provided technical and managerial support to the rural and district (peri-urban) municipalities in the coordination and implementation of pro-employment and climate smart infrastructure development. The ILO developed guidelines and productivity norms for greening EPWP in March 2020, based on the previously conducted ILO viability study. Regarding the infrastructure led recovery strategy, the ILO developed a discussion paper in May 2020 on how to increase the labour intensity of infrastructure investments in economic recovery, learning from international and regional experiences. The ILO also supported the development of an on-line platform for technical, managerial and business training related to employment intensive infrastructure works incorporating social safeguards including occupational safety and health (OSH) measures and COVID-19 prevention. The target for online training included personnel of local authorities, small-scale entrepreneurs, youth, women and people with disabilities. In addition, the ILO provided technical, managerial and business training at the national, provincial and rural district levels, benefiting some 837 officials of which 43% were women.
